why: Protection of ownership (no one deprived of his property save as the law provides); the owner's right to recover the property would rest on it beside 674. The civil-code text view holds 674 only from the ownership chapter.
Publication as a condition of the transfer of real rights; element e1 (ownership proven by a published title) and the catalogue document 'published title deed' would cite it.
Acquisitive prescription by long possession, the occupier's main defence to an ownership-based eviction; a boundary or warning would cite it (open point o2).
Shorter acquisitive prescription with just title and good faith, read around 827 (open point o2).
Fruits owed by a possessor in good or bad faith; the occupation indemnity (request r2) could rest on it instead of tort (open point o9).
Duty of the possessor in bad faith to return the fruits received or neglected; alternative ground of request r2 (open point o9).
Works built or planted by a third party on the owner's land, the owner's choice to keep or remove them (open point o5).
Criminal trespass on real property, for the criminal exit on the same facts (open point o8).
The bailiff's power to draw up records of findings and their evidential force, for document doc2 (open point o7).
